name: Russ Thorsen
languages: Norwegian (his grandmother's, enough to understand old people saying things they think he can't)
equipment: Heavy coat: a red-and-black wool Mackinaw, patched at both elbows, with a Wisconsin bowhunting license pinned to the back
Hunting bow: a sixty-pound recurve he made himself from Osage orange in 1958
A back quiver of broadheads and a bow stringer
Hunting rifle: a bolt-action .30-06 with a scope, in a fleece case behind the pickup seat
A ring of keys to Pine Lodge on Big Sand Lake, Vilas County, which he has kept for nineteen years
A topographic map of Kinnick County with a year of pencil marks on it: everywhere he has looked for Dr. Gessler
A thermos of coffee and a sack of his own sandwiches (he has started bringing his own food without knowing why)
Pickup: a 1966 Chevrolet half-ton, green, with a CB radio and a gun rack
features: Been Here Before (Survivor origin: advantage on initiative; when a fight or a fright begins he always knows the nearest way out; once per long rest, when he fails a saving throw, including a fear check, he rerolls it and must use the new roll; the first time each scenario he meets a horror like the one he survived, the GM tells him one way it is the same. He survived the cold at the Chosin Reservoir in Korea in 1950, and the GM will tell him what the cold in the corn has in common with it)

Know Your Quarry (Hunter: after an hour studying a creature's sign he can declare it his quarry; advantage on Survival checks to track it and Perception checks to find it, he always knows which way it went from a place where he found its sign, and once on each of his turns when he hits it with a weapon it takes an extra 1d6 damage of the weapon's type; not part of the damage on his sheet)

Fieldcraft (Hunter: he can't become lost in woods, fields, marsh or hill country except by something that is not natural, and moves at a normal pace while moving stealthily outdoors; in a short rest he can set a snare, a tripwire bell or a pit that warns him of anything coming within 30 ft of camp)

Cold Focus (Hunter, 2nd level: when he fails a fear check against his quarry he still gains the Dread, but has advantage on his next attack against it before the end of his next turn; when he succeeds on one, he can move up to half his speed without provoking opportunity attacks)
Way of the Hunt: Hunter of the Uncanny (Hunter, 3rd level: once he has declared a supernatural creature his quarry, the GM tells him one of its rules about what hurts it or bars it)

Every Path and Gate (Groundskeeper background: given a day on any grounds he knows every path, outbuilding, gate and gap, where the drains run and where the ground has been disturbed; he notices fresh digging without a check; caretakers and sextons talk to him and he can usually find out who has keys to what)
traits: Way of the Hunt: Hunter of the Uncanny

personality.traits: I say about ten words an hour and mean all of them. I notice weather, tracks and people's hands. I am patient in a way that makes other people nervous.
personality.ideals: You don't leave a man in the woods. Not a deer you've wounded, not a client who didn't come back to the truck.
personality.bonds: Howard Gessler, who hired me as his guide in 1964 and became my friend, and who walked out of the diner in Hollow Fork at six in the morning on 3 October 1973 to look at deer on the rim of the Hollow and didn't come back. His wife, Doris, who writes to me every month and has stopped asking.
personality.flaws: I have come back to Hollow Fork every month for a year, and every time I sit at Elsie's counter, and every time she has my coffee poured, and I don't like how much I look forward to it.

appearance: Forty-four, long and lean and weathered, with a grey crew cut, pale blue eyes that never stop moving, two fingers on his left hand that don't bend all the way since Korea, and a red-and-black Mackinaw he has worn every fall for twenty years.
backstory: Russell Thorsen grew up on a cutover farm near Rhinelander, enlisted in the Marines at eighteen and was at the Chosin Reservoir in the winter of 1950, where the cold killed more of his company than the enemy did; he came home with frostbitten fingers and a refusal to talk about it. Since 1955 he has been caretaker of Pine Lodge, a hunting and fishing lodge on Big Sand Lake in Vilas County, and in the fall he guides bowhunters. Dr. Howard Gessler, an Evanston surgeon, hired him in 1964 and they hunted together every October for nine years, from the Northwoods to the Driftless. In October 1973 they came to Hollow Fork for the coulee deer; on the morning of 3 October Howard walked out of the diner to scout the rim of the Hollow, alone, and never came back. His car turned up at the La Crosse Greyhound depot two weeks later with his bow case in the trunk. The sheriff called it a man leaving his marriage. Russ has driven down to Hollow Fork once a month since, walked the coulees, talked to everyone, and eaten a great many slices of Elsie's pie. Everyone in Hollow Fork is very fond of him. (Hook: the client. He is the alternate pencilled under Dawn's name in the Book; see hs-scenario-002. He has been fed by the town for a year and does not know what that means.)
